title: Ringed koszul reflector
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site with a sheaf of commutative rings $\mathcal O$, and let $b_1,\ldots,b_r$ be global sections (the finite list may be empty). Put $\mathcal J=(b_1,\ldots,b_r)\mathcal O$. For $N\in D(\mathcal O)$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-abstract-derived-category], let $Q_m=\bigotimes_{j=1}^r[\mathcal O\xrightarrow{b_j^m}\mathcal O]$ in degrees $[-r,0]$ [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves], with transition multiplication by $b_j$ in degree $-1$ and identity in degree $0$ in each factor. Interpret $R\lim$ on the strict tower $N\otimes^L Q_m$ as the total right derived inverse limit, computed by a K-injective resolution of strict towers [def-pur-kinjective-complex, def-weil-derived-limit]. The degree-zero maps $\mathcal O\to Q_m$ induce $\eta_N:N\to R\lim_m(N\otimes^L_{\mathcal O}Q_m)$. The latter object is locally derived $\mathcal J$-complete: for every $U$ and $f\in\mathcal J(U)$, its restriction has zero derived internal Hom from $\mathcal O_U[1/f]$ [def-pur-derived-internal-hom], where localization means sheafified sectionwise localization. For every object $L$ satisfying this local condition, composition with $\eta_N$ gives a bijection $\operatorname{Hom}(R\lim_m(N\otimes^L Q_m),L)\to\operatorname{Hom}(N,L)$. Consequently $\eta_N$ is an isomorphism if and only if $N$ satisfies this local condition. The construction and its unit are natural in $N$.

source.place: Tags 099B (lemma-derived-completion) and 0A0E (lemma-derived-completion-koszul); the local completeness condition is Tag 0999 (definition-derived-complete).

proof.text: Write $C=C_b$ and $\epsilon:C\to\mathcal O$ as in the Cech/Koszul comparison. Put $F(N)=R\mathcal Hom(C,N)$ and $\eta^C_N=\epsilon^*:N\cong R\mathcal Hom(\mathcal O,N)\to F(N)$. Let $T(N)$ denote the strict derived limit in the item. The comparison gives a natural isomorphism $\theta_N:F(N)\to T(N)$ and the equality $\theta_N\eta^C_N=\eta_N$. Its forward maps $(1,b_j)$ dualize to $(b_j,1)$, so they are exactly the specified inverse maps, not a different Koszul system. The strict-tower theorem fixes the total derived inverse-limit interpretation, without assuming exact sheaf products.

Fix an object $U$ and an index $i$. Apply the localization/internal-Hom calculation to $P=C$ on the slice. It gives
$$R\mathcal Hom_{\mathcal O_U}(\mathcal O_U[1/b_i],F(N)|_U)\cong R\mathcal Hom_{\mathcal O_U}(\mathcal O_U[1/b_i]\otimes^L C|_U,N|_U).$$
The first argument on the right is the ordinary Cech complex with coefficients $\mathcal O_U[1/b_i]$. It is explicitly contractible. Index a degree-$q$ component by a sorted subset $S$ of size $q$. Define $(hx)_S=0$ when $i\in S$, and $(hx)_S=(-1)^t x_{S\cup\{i\}}$ otherwise, where $t$ is the number of elements of $S$ less than $i$; identify the two localizations using invertibility of $b_i$. If $i\in S$, only the term deleting $i$ survives in $dh$, with sign $(-1)^t(-1)^t=1$. If $i\notin S$, the term deleting $i$ in $hd$ is $x_S$, and every other deletion term cancels the corresponding term of $dh$ with opposite sign. Thus $dh+hd=1$, including the empty-subset degree-zero component. Therefore the displayed derived internal Hom is zero for every generator on every slice. This argument is about $F(N)$ for arbitrary $N$; it assumes no completeness of $N$.

proof.text: Apply the vanishing-elements ideal lemma with $K=F(N)$. Step 2 places all restricted $b_i$ in the ideal sheaf $S_K$. Since $\mathcal J$ is the smallest ideal subsheaf containing those sections, $\mathcal J\subset S_K$. More explicitly, a section $f\in\mathcal J(U)$ is a finite sum of multiples of the $b_i$ on a covering of $U$; ideal closure gives vanishing there and the sheaf clause gives it on $U$. Consequently $F(N)$ is locally derived $\mathcal J$-complete. By $\theta_N$ and its slice compatibility, so is $T(N)$. For $r=0$, $\mathcal J=0$, and the same ideal lemma contains the zero section, whose localization is the zero sheaf.

Verify the local-description hypothesis of the existing general augmented-Cech completion theorem for the explicit $C$. The ideal sheaf $\mathcal J$ is finite type because the global list is finite. On each slice, $C|_U$ is exactly the alternating localization complex of the restricted $b_i$, with its augmentation. For any other generating list $c_1,\ldots,c_s$ on that slice, apply the existence clause of the same theorem to the small ringed site $\mathcal C/U$ and its ideal $\mathcal J|_U$. This site has terminal object $(U,\mathrm{id})$. At that object the theorem supplies a single augmented complex $K_U$ and augmentation-compatible isomorphisms $\alpha_b:C_b|_U\to K_U$ and $\alpha_c:C_c\to K_U$. Their composite $\alpha_b^{-1}\alpha_c:C_c\to C|_U$ respects augmentations. Thus $C$ has every local description required by the theorem, even if the two lists generate the same ideal only as sheaves. Apply its reflection clause to $C\to\mathcal O$ to obtain the correctly typed bijection
$$\Phi_{N,L}:\operatorname{Hom}(F(N),L)\longrightarrow\operatorname{Hom}(N,L),\qquad u\longmapsto u\eta^C_N$$
for every locally complete $L$. It also states that $\eta^C_L$ is an isomorphism for such $L$. This uses both explicit clauses of an existing general theorem; it asserts no tensor-Hom adjunction with $F(N)$ in its first slot.

source.place: Tags 099D (lemma-all-rings), 099E (lemma-global-extended-cech-complex), and 099F (proposition-derived-completion), applied to the globally generated ideal.

proof.text: Define the inverse for the claimed mapping bijection as follows. Given $a:N\to L$, let $u=\Phi_{N,L}^{-1}(a):F(N)\to L$, the unique map whose composition with $\eta^C_N$ is $a$, whose existence and uniqueness are supplied in Step 4. Set $v=u\theta_N^{-1}:T(N)\to L$. Then $v\eta_N=u\theta_N^{-1}\theta_N\eta^C_N=a$. Conversely, for $v:T(N)\to L$, the morphism $v\theta_N$ composes with $\eta^C_N$ to $v\eta_N$, so uniqueness in Step 4 gives $\Phi_{N,L}^{-1}(v\eta_N)=v\theta_N$. Multiplying by $\theta_N^{-1}$ recovers $v$. These two equations prove both inverse identities and retain the prescribed tower unit.

source.place: Tags 099F (proposition-derived-completion) and 0A0E (lemma-derived-completion-koszul), with the augmentation-compatible unit comparison.

proof.text: If $N$ is locally complete, Step 4 gives that $\eta^C_N$ is an isomorphism, and hence so is $\eta_N=\theta_N\eta^C_N$. If $\eta_N$ is an isomorphism, the already proved completeness of $T(N)$ in Step 3 is carried to $N$ on every slice by this isomorphism and derived internal-Hom functoriality. This proves both implications without confusing a retraction with a two-sided inverse.

source.place: Tags 099B and 099F, isomorphism on complete objects; completeness of the output proved in Steps 2–3.

proof.text: For $a:N\to N'$, functoriality gives $F(a)\eta^C_N=\eta^C_{N'}a$. Naturality of $\theta$ gives $T(a)\theta_N=\theta_{N'}F(a)$. Therefore $T(a)\eta_N=T(a)\theta_N\eta^C_N=\theta_{N'}F(a)\eta^C_N=\eta_{N'}a$. The comparison lemma also makes the strict tower independent of the complex representative. This proves naturality of both the construction and its unit, including on slices.
